concept.name: Taxonomy
concept.definition: A controlled vocabulary organized as a hierarchy of broader/narrower (parent/child) concepts, used to classify content consistently. ANSI/NISO Z39.19 defines conventions for constructing, formatting, and managing such vocabularies — including lists, synonym rings, taxonomies, and thesauri — as knowledge organization systems.
concept.intuition: A family tree of categories: every item gets a place, and the place tells you what more general and more specific categories it belongs to.
concept.mechanics: Concepts are arranged by generic relationships (a futures contract IS-A derivative), each concept carries a preferred term, and items are tagged with the most specific applicable node. Retrieval can then expand or narrow along the hierarchy.
concept.failure_modes: Breaks down on items that genuinely belong to multiple parents or straddle categories, and becomes stale when the domain innovates faster than the hierarchy is maintained. Forcing mutually exclusive buckets onto continuous phenomena creates arbitrary boundaries.
concept.misconceptions: A taxonomy is weaker than an ontology: it captures only hierarchical (broader/narrower) structure, not arbitrary typed relations, constraints, or formal semantics. Being in the same taxonomic branch does not imply functional equivalence.
concept.example: This library's 29 canonical domains form a taxonomy of trading concepts: 'Order types' is narrower than 'Trading mechanics', and every concept is assigned exactly one domain.

citations.source: ANSI/NISO Z39.19-2005 (R2010), Guidelines for the Construction, Format, and Management of Monolingual Controlled Vocabularies
